summary: An Indologist and linguist, Peter von Bohlen studied at the Gelehrtenschule des Johanneums, Halle-Wittenberg, Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp, and Bonn under Georg Wilhelm Freytag. In 1826, he became an außerordentlicher Professor at the University of Königsberg.

Peter von Bradke was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Dorpat under Leo Meyer, Tübingen, Leipzig, and Giessen, also studying under Rudolf von Roth. He completed his Habilitation at Giessen and held a post there from 1886 to 1896.

Working in Indology and Buddhist studies, Petra Kieffer-Pülz was a pupil of Heinz Bechert (attested 1996). Around 1993, she served as a Research Fellow at the Academy of Sciences and Literature Mainz.

Specializing in Tibetology and Indology, Petra Maurer studied under Dieter Schuh and Dunchu Sonam Dorje. She held posts at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2013), University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (2017), and LMU Munich (attested 2018).

Pham Thi Tuyet Tam is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed an MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, supervised by Phra Maha Somboon Vuddhikaro and Sanu Mahatthanadull (both attested 2017).

Phanit Jetjiravat specializes in Buddhist studies and earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, advised by Phra Suthithammanuwat, Veerachart Nimanong, and Paetpong Worapongpichet.

Philip A. Kuhn was a sinologist and historian educated at Harvard, SOAS, and Georgetown. He served in the US Armed Forces and held academic posts at the University of Chicago, Harvard University, and the Fairbank Center for Chinese Studies.

A scholar of religious studies, Philip A. Mellor completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Manchester by 1989. Attested in 2010, he was Professor of Religion and Social Theory and Head of the School of Humanities at Leeds.

A scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, Philip B. Yampolsky studied under Yoshitaka Iriya. He served as Adjunct Associate Professor and East Asian Library Librarian, then Lecturer, at Columbia University, and chaired the Numata Center (1991–1996).
Specializing in religious studies and Indology, Philip Deslippe pursued his PhD at the University of California, Santa Barbara, where he also held a post as a teaching associate (both attested 2020).

Philip L. Quinn was a philosopher and religious studies scholar educated at Georgetown, Delaware, and Pittsburgh. He held major academic posts at Brown University from around 1970 to 1985 and at the University of Notre Dame from roughly 1985 to 2004.

Philip Whalen was a Buddhist and religious studies figure educated at Reed College and under Richard Baker. He was a visiting poet at Naropa University, resident teacher at South Ridge Zendo, and abbot of Hartford Street Zen Center (1991–1996).

An Indologist and philosopher, Philipp A. Maas earned his PhD at the University of Bonn under Claus Vogel and Albrecht Wezler. His appointments include Bonn, the University of Vienna, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and Leipzig University.

Philippe Turenne specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at McGill University under G. Victor Sōgen Hori and studied under several teachers including Khenpo Palden Sherab, Richard P. Hayes, and Kameshwar Nath Mishra.

Philippe-Édouard Foucaux worked in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies, studying under Eugène Burnouf. He was Professeur de Tibétain at INALCO from 1854, Professeur de Sanskrit at Collège de France from 1857 to 1894, and an American Oriental Society member.

Phillip B. Zarrilli was a scholar in Indology and other fields. He held academic posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from approximately 1979 to 1999 and at the University of Exeter from around 2000 to 2020.

Specializing in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, Phillip E. Bloom earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2013) under the doctoral supervision of Eugene Y. Wang, Yukio Lippit, and James Robson.

Phra Brahmagunabhorn is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned BAs from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University and Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University. He served as Dean of Buddhist Studies and Deputy Vice Rector at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2012).

Working in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Phra Brahmapundit served as Rector of Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (~1997–2018). He was also President of the International Association of Buddhist Universities (~2007) and Chairperson/President of the International Council for the Day of Vesak (~2004).

A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, Phra Kiattisak Ponampon earned an MA at the University of Otago supervised by Xiaohuan Zhao, Will Sweetman, and Elizabeth Guthrie, and studied under teachers including Jinhua Chen and John Kieschnick.
